The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6453a6d9ab0cf566), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. statement: For the integers m, p and the finite list just specified, there is a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold X, constructed without Assumption 2.1, with the following properties. It has a regular cover with deck group Fm, whose block graph is the Cayley tree of Fm. Each block is a four-dimensional one-handlebody on the p extra letters. Its exposed boundary piece is Kv ∼ = ( #p (S1 × S2 ) ) \ int ν(L2m), where L2m is a 2m-component unlink in a ball. The port meridians and the extra letters freely generate π1Kv. At every join, the meridian on one side is the longitude on the other. There is a finite family of framed grope bodies with boundary in these pieces, equivariant in the cover, realizing the list (2.3). If Assumption 2.1 holds, there are equivariant cuts, with compact quotient, having connected vertex pieces Vv and connected edge three-manifolds Ye. Each Ye has as its entire boundary the prescribed join torus. Every corresponding three-slot grope word is trivial in π1Vv. In the index-two parity quotient, these cuts give two connected vertex pieces A, B and 2m connected oriented edge pieces Y1, . . . , Y2m. Their ambient manifold X2 is homotopy equivalent to the graph with two vertices and 2m edges, with p additional circles at each vertex. For any characteristic-zero field k, difference of restrictions gives H2 (A; k) ⊕ H2 (B; k) ∼ = − − → 2m ⨁ i=1 H2 (Yi; k). (2.4) In degree one it is surjective, and restricts to an isomorphism on the kernel of evaluation on the p extra loops at each vertex. At each boundary torus choose the two original coordinate loops αi, βi so that αi has nonzero image in H1(Yi; k) and βi has zero image. Such a choice is possible: one of the original coordinate directions, not just an arbitrary slope, is killed. Call the endpoint where βi is a longitude the plus endpoint; there αi is the port meridian. There are exactly m edges with plus endpoint A. After numbering these as 1, . . . , m, the finite relation list includes, at A, all the required three-slot relations on any three distinct αi, and, at B, those on the corresponding βi, with independent conjugations by C.
